(No. 21-418, opinion by Justice Gorsuch; 597 U.S. 507).

title: Supreme Court: Concepcion v. United States
summary: Section 404(b) of the First Step Act of 2018, 132 Stat. 5222, allows district courts to consider intervening changes of law or fact in exercising their discretion to reduce a sentence. (No. 20-1650, opinion by Justice Sotomayor; 597 U.S. 481).

title: Supreme Court: Xiulu Ruan v. United States
summary: For the crime of prescribing controlled substances outside the usual course of professional practice in violation of 21 U. S. C. §841, the mens rea “knowingly or intentionally” applies to the statute’s “except as authorized” clause. (No. 20-1410, opinion by Justice Breyer; 597 U.S. 450).

title: Supreme Court: Becerra v. Empire Health Foundation, For Valley Hospital Medical Center
summary: For purposes of calculating the Medicare fraction—one of two fractions the Medicare program uses to adjust the rates paid to hospitals that serve a higher-than-usual percentage of low-income patients—those individuals “entitled to [Medicare Part A] benefits” are all those qualifying for the program, regardless of whether they receive Medicare payments for part or all of a hospital stay. (No. 20-1312, opinion by Justice Kagan; 597 U.S. 424).

title: Supreme Court: Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization
summary: The Constitution does not confer a right to abortion; Roe v. Wade, 410 U. S. 113, and Planned Parenthood of Southeastern Pa. v. Casey, 505 U. S. 833, are overruled; the authority to regulate abortion is returned to the people and their elected representatives. (No. 19-1392, opinion by Justice Alito; 597 U.S. 215).

title: Supreme Court: Berger v. North Carolina State Conference of the NAACP
summary: The speaker of the North Carolina State House of Representatives and the president pro tempore of the North Carolina State Senate are entitled to intervene in this litigation challenging North Carolina’s voter-ID law. (No. 21-248, opinion by Justice Gorsuch; 597 U.S. 179).

title: Supreme Court: Nance v. Ward
summary: Title 42 U. S. C. §1983 is the procedural vehicle appropriate for a prisoner’s method-of-execution claim even if an order granting the relief requested would necessitate a change in state law. (No. 21-439, opinion by Justice Kagan; 597 U.S. 159).

title: Supreme Court: Vega v. Tekoh
summary: A violation of the prophylactic rules described in Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U. S. 436, does not provide a basis for a claim under 42 U. S. C. §1983. (No. 21-499, opinion by Justice Alito; 597 U.S. 134).

title: Supreme Court: New York State Rifle & Pistol Assn., Inc. v. Bruen
summary: New York’s proper-cause requirement for obtaining an unrestricted license to carry a concealed firearm violates the Fourteenth Amendment in that it prevents law-abiding citizens with ordinary self-defense needs from exercising their Second Amendment right to keep and bear arms. (No. 20-843, opinion by Justice Thomas; 597 U.S. 1).

title: Supreme Court: Marietta Memorial Hospital Employee Health Benefit Plan v. DaVita Inc.
summary: The Medicare Secondary Payer statute does not authorize disparate-impact liability, and the Marietta Plan’s coverage terms for outpatient dialysis do not violate 42 U. S. C. §1395y(b)(1)(C) because those terms apply uniformly to all covered individuals. (No. 20-1641, opinion by Justice Kavanaugh; 596 U.S. 880).

title: Supreme Court: United States v. Taylor
summary: Attempted Hobbs Act robbery does not qualify as a “crime of violence” under 18 U. S. C. §924(c)(3)(A) because no element of the offense requires proof that the defendant used, attempted to use, or threatened to use force. (No. 20-1459, opinion by Justice Gorsuch; 596 U.S. 845).

title: Supreme Court: United States v. Washington
summary: Washington’s workers’ compensation law is unconstitutional under the Supremacy Clause because it facially discriminates against the Federal Government and does not fall within the scope of the federal waiver of immunity contained in 40 U. S. C. §3172. (No. 21-404, opinion by Justice Breyer; 596 U.S. 832).

title: Supreme Court: Shoop v. Twyford
summary: A transportation order that allows a prisoner to search for new evidence—in this case an order compelling the State to transport Mr. Twyford to a medical facility for neurological testing—is not “necessary or appropriate in aid of” a federal court’s adjudication of a habeas corpus action when the prisoner has not shown that the desired evidence would be admissible in connection with a particular claim for relief. (No. 21-511, opinion by Chief Justice Roberts; 596 U.S. 811).

title: Supreme Court: Carson v. Makin
summary: Maine’s “nonsectarian” requirement for otherwise generally available tuition assistance payments to parents who live in school districts that do not operate a secondary school of their own violates the Free Exercise Clause of the First Amendment. (No. 20-1088, opinion by Chief Justice Roberts; 596 U.S. 767).

title: Supreme Court: Arizona v. City and County of San Francisco
summary: Certiorari dismissed as improvidently granted. (No. 20-1775, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 596 U.S. 763).

title: Supreme Court: George v. McDonough
summary: The invalidation of a Department of Veterans Affairs regulation after a veteran’s benefits decision becomes final cannot support a claim for collateral relief permitting revision of that decision based on “clear and unmistakable error” under 38 U. S. C. §§5109A and 7111. (No. 21-234, opinion by Justice Barrett; 596 U.S. 740).

title: Supreme Court: American Hospital Assn. v. Becerra
summary: The Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement, and Modernization Act of 2003 does not preclude judicial review of the reimbursement rates set by the Department of Health and Human Services for certain outpatient prescription drugs that hospitals provide to Medicare patients; in this case, because HHS did not conduct a survey of hospitals’ acquisition costs in 2018 and 2019, its decision to vary reimbursement rates only for 340B hospitals in those years was unlawful. (No. 20-1114, opinion by Justice Kavanaugh; 596 U.S. 724).

title: Supreme Court: Ysleta del Sur Pueblo v. Texas
summary: The federal legislation at issue—the Ysleta del Sur and Alabama and Coushatta Indian Tribes of Texas Restoration Act—bans as a matter of federal law on tribal lands only those gaming activities also banned in Texas. (No. 20-493, opinion by Justice Gorsuch; 596 U.S. 685).

title: Supreme Court: Golan v. Saada
summary: A court is not categorically required to examine all possible ameliorative measures before denying a Hague Convention petition for return of a child to a foreign country once the court has found that return would expose the child to a grave risk of harm. (No. 20-1034, opinion by Justice Sotomayor; 596 U.S. 666).

title: Supreme Court: Viking River Cruises, Inc. v. Moriana
summary: The Federal Arbitration Act preempts a rule of California law that invalidates contractual waivers of the right to assert representative claims under “PAGA”—California’s Labor Code Private Attorneys General Act of 2004—insofar as that rule precludes division of PAGA actions into individual and non-individual claims through an agreement to arbitrate. (No. 20-1573, opinion by Justice Alito; 596 U.S. 639).

title: Supreme Court: ZF Automotive U. S., Inc. v. Luxshare, Ltd.
summary: Although 28 U. S. C. §1782(a) permits a district court to order discovery “for use in a proceeding in a foreign or international tribunal,” only a governmental or intergovernmental adjudicative body may qualify as such a tribunal, and the arbitration panels in these cases are not such adjudicative bodies. (No. 21-401, opinion by Justice Barrett; 596 U.S. 619).

title: Supreme Court: Denezpi v. United States
summary: The Double Jeopardy Clause does not bar successive prosecutions of distinct offenses arising from a single act, even if a single sovereign prosecutes them. (No. 20-7622, opinion by Justice Barrett; 596 U.S. 591).

title: Supreme Court: Johnson v. Arteaga-Martinez
summary: Title 8 U. S. C. §1231(a)(6) does not require the Government to provide noncitizens detained for six months with bond hearings in which the Government bears the burden of proving, by clear and convincing evidence, that a noncitizen poses a flight risk or a danger to the community. (No. 19-896, opinion by Justice Sotomayor; 596 U.S. 573).

title: Supreme Court: Garland v. Gonzalez
summary: Title 8 U. S. C. §1252(f)(1)—which generally strips lower courts of “jurisdiction or authority” to “enjoin or restrain the operation of ” certain provisions of the Immigration and Nationality Act—deprived the District Courts of jurisdiction in these cases to entertain respondents’ requests for class-wide injunctive relief. (No. 20-322, opinion by Justice Alito; 596 U.S. 543).

title: Supreme Court: Kemp v. United States
summary: The term “mistake” in Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60(b)(1) includes a judge’s errors of law; because Kemp’s motion alleged such an error, it was cognizable under Rule 60(b)(1) and untimely under Rule 60(c)’s 1-year limitations period. (No. 21-5726, opinion by Justice Thomas; 596 U.S. 528).

title: Supreme Court: Egbert v. Boule
summary: The authority of a court to imply a cause of action under Bivens v. Six Unknown Fed. Narcotics Agents, 403 U. S. 388, does not extend to either Boule’s Fourth Amendment excessive-force claim or his First Amendment retaliation claim. (No. 21-147, opinion by Justice Thomas; 596 U.S. 482).

title: Supreme Court: Siegel v. Fitzgerald
summary: Congress’ enactment of a significant fee increase that exempted debtors in two States violated the uniformity requirement of the Bankruptcy Clause. (No. 21-441, opinion by Justice Sotomayor; 596 U.S. 464).

title: Supreme Court: Southwest Airlines Co. v. Saxon
summary: Airplane cargo loaders and ramp supervisors who, like petitioner Saxon, frequently load and unload airplane cargo belong to a “class of workers engaged in foreign or interstate commerce” exempt from the Federal Arbitration Act’s coverage. (No. 21-309, opinion by Justice Thomas; 596 U.S. 450).

title: Supreme Court: Gallardo v. Marstiller
summary: The Medicaid Act permits a State to seek reimbursement from settlement payments allocated for future medical care. (No. 20-1263, opinion by Justice Thomas; 596 U.S. 420).
